open_risks: The eleven Phase 1 auth operations are implemented and tested but not yet frozen: they need the joint contract review that manual.docx 27.2 puts before implementation. Person One built to the contract as written rather than waiting, so a change agreed at that review is a change to both the contract and the implementation, in one pull request.

PLUG's own access and refresh tokens are opaque and resolved against the sessions table on every request (ADR-006). That is one indexed read and one last_used_at write per authenticated call. It has not been load-tested; measure before assuming it holds.

Phone verification has no delivery channel until Phase 3 (ADR-007). POST /v1/auth/phone/start answers 503 dependency_unavailable in staging. The brute-force and rate-limit cases are proved by automated tests, not yet against real staging, and G1 should record that.

Sign in with Apple needs the capability enabled on App ID com.abubakarsidiq01.plug.app101 in the Apple Developer portal before a device build will sign. The entitlement file is committed; the portal side is a manual step nobody has taken yet.

PLUG_IDENTITY_PEPPER is now required by the db and staging profiles, including for local ./dev databaseTest runs. It keys the stored phone, Apple-subject and one-time-code hashes, so rotating it makes every existing identity unrecognisable. It has no secret-storage home yet beyond .env.local and the CI workflow.

No account type in Phase 1 can be granted the admin scope, so every route under /v1/admin is refused. AdminStepUpAuthorization is in place ahead of the first admin route, but nothing exercises the allow path yet — that arrives with the admin identity model in Phase 5.

The consent links point at PLUG_WEB_URL plus /terms and /privacy. Person Two owns those routes (P1-TWO), no production domain has been decided, and an unset value shows the labels as plain text rather than as links that go nowhere.

Operational health routes reject requests carrying tunnel/proxy forwarding headers by design (SecurityConfiguration.directProbeOnly()). GET /health/ready correctly returns HTTP 401 through the public tunnel; GET /health and the POST /v1/requests cases pass. Confirmed from both Person One's Mac/iPhone and, on 2026-09-22, Person Two's own Windows PC — the ADR-005 deferral for her own-machine API run is resolved.

AWS staging is deferred (ADR-004) — no budget available right now, even for the near-$0/month minimal design in docs/runbooks/aws-staging-setup.md. The Phase 0 connected checkpoint uses a cloudflared Quick Tunnel instead; revisit AWS no later than Phase 3, when Twilio needs a stable (non-rotating) webhook URL a Quick Tunnel can't provide.

Backend has no Redis dependency or Redis readiness check, even though infra/compose.yml and docker-compose.yml provision Redis. The Phase 1 rate limits are counted in one process's memory through FixedWindowLimiter, which is correct for one instance and wrong the moment there are two. Wire Redis in before the backend is ever run as more than one process.
